title: canVoid grants void to every non-admin and denies it to an admin listed first
evidence: Array.indexOf returns -1 when the item is absent (truthy) and 0 when it is first (falsy). app.js:2 signs in sam with roles ["viewer","billing"], so canVoid(user) is true for a user with no admin role. A user whose roles are ["admin"] gets 0, so canVoid is false and the Void button silently does nothing for the one role allowed to use it. Traced from the code; the sandbox refused shell execution, so not run.
failing_case: Open the page as sam (roles viewer, billing) and click Void invoice: canVoid returns true, and app.js:33 POSTs /api/invoices/void. Sign in as roles ["admin"]: indexOf returns 0, canVoid returns false, the click returns at app.js:32 with no message.
remediation: Use user.roles.includes("admin") and return the boolean directly. Add a test with roles [], ["admin"] and ["viewer","admin"]. Enforce the same rule on the server (see the trust-boundary finding).

title: validQuantity accepts empty, blank, negative, fractional and exponent quantities
evidence: The value arrives as a string (app.js:17). isNaN("") and isNaN("  ") are false because both coerce to 0, so both pass. "-5", "1.5", "1e3" and "Infinity" are also not NaN. app.js:20 then stores Number(qtyText).
failing_case: Leave Quantity empty, enter a price of 5, press Add line: the line is stored with qty 0 and the total is 0.00. Enter -5 with price 20: the line adds -100.00 to the total and is posted in the invoice. Enter 1e9: a billion units.
remediation: Validate with /^[1-9]\d*$/ (or Number.isInteger(n) && n > 0 with a sane upper bound) on the trimmed string, and re-check on the server.

title: tooSoon never fires because lastSend is never updated, so the send guard is dead and invoices can be double-sent
evidence: lastSend is declared at guards.js:22 and read here, but no line anywhere assigns it (grep of the four files shows only the declaration and this read). Date.now() - 0 is always far above 1000, so tooSoon() at app.js:25 is always false. app.js:24-29 has no in-flight flag, no disabled button, and the lines array is not cleared after success, so a second send posts the same lines again.
failing_case: Click Send invoice twice within a second, or click again while the first fetch is pending: two POSTs to /api/invoices carry the same lines, so the client is invoiced twice. A slow network makes this easy.
remediation: Set lastSend = Date.now() when a send starts, or better, disable the button while the request is in flight and send an idempotency key so the server drops a repeat.

quote: const user = { name: "sam", roles: ["viewer", "billing"] };  // the signed-in user
title: Roles are a client-side literal, so the browser alone decides who may void
evidence: The signed-in user and their roles are hardcoded in client code. canVoid is the only permission check in these four files. The void request carries no credentials or role data of its own. Anyone can run user.roles.push("admin") in the console or call the endpoint directly. Whether the server checks is not visible in the payload, so this cannot be confirmed or ruled out. Traced.
failing_case: In the console, run fetch("/api/invoices/void", {method:"POST"}) as a viewer. If the server relies on the UI check, the invoice is voided.
remediation: Load the user from the session, treat canVoid as display only (hide the button), and make the void endpoint check the role on the server.

title: price > 0 accepts Infinity and huge values, which then post as null
evidence: Number("Infinity") and Number("1e999") are Infinity, and Infinity > 0 is true. render() then shows Infinity.toFixed(2) as "Infinity" and the total as Infinity. JSON.stringify(lines) at app.js:26 turns Infinity into null. Traced.
failing_case: Enter price 1e999 with quantity 1 and add the line: the total shows Infinity, and Send invoice posts {"price":null}.
remediation: Require Number.isFinite(price) && price > 0, cap the range, and round to cents.

title: Rejected line input gives no message, focus move or marker
evidence: The submit handler returns silently when quantity or price fails. The inputs have no aria-invalid, no error text and no type/min attributes (index.html:16,18). The user sees the Add line button do nothing. Traced.
failing_case: Type abc in Quantity and press Add line: nothing changes and nothing is announced. A screen reader user cannot tell why the line did not appear.
remediation: Show a message next to the field (for example "Quantity must be a whole number of 1 or more"), set aria-invalid and link it with aria-describedby, and move focus to the first bad field.

quote: const res = await fetch("/api/invoices", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(lines) });
title: fetch rejection is not caught on Send and Void, so network failure is silent
evidence: app.js:26 and app.js:33 await fetch with no try/catch. Only a non-2xx response reaches the alert. A rejected fetch (offline, DNS, CORS, abort) throws inside the async handler as an unhandled promise rejection, and the user sees nothing. Traced.
failing_case: Go offline and click Send invoice: the console shows an unhandled rejection, no alert appears, and the user cannot tell whether the invoice went out, so they may retry or assume it was sent.
remediation: Wrap each fetch in try/catch, show "Could not reach the server. The invoice was not sent. Check your connection and try again.", and keep the data.

title: Successful send shows nothing, leaves the lines in place and counts into a variable no one reads
evidence: After res.ok the handler only increments sentCount. sentCount is never read anywhere in the four files. There is no confirmation, no clearing of lines, and no disabled state for the button. The void handler (app.js:34) has the same gap on success. Traced.
failing_case: Click Send invoice on a good connection: the page looks unchanged, the user cannot tell if it worked, and clicks again. That posts the same lines a second time, as the tooSoon guard is dead.
remediation: Show a status message in a role=status region ("Invoice sent"), clear or lock the lines, disable the buttons while a request runs, and remove sentCount or use it.

title: Void is irreversible, has no confirmation and sends no invoice identifier
evidence: The Void button posts with no body, so the request does not say which invoice to void. There is no confirm step, no undo and no success message. Combined with the inverted role check (guards.js:10), any signed-in non-admin reaches it. Traced.
failing_case: Click Void invoice by mistake next to Send invoice (both buttons are adjacent, index.html:23-24): the server voids whatever it treats as current, with no prompt.
remediation: Send the invoice id in the body, ask for confirmation naming the invoice, and show the outcome.

title: escapeHtml leaves double and single quotes unescaped, but app.js uses it inside a quoted attribute
evidence: app.js:8 builds title="${escapeHtml(l.client)}" and assigns it with innerHTML. escapeHtml encodes only & < >. A double quote in the client name closes the attribute and lets the input add its own attributes. Traced.
failing_case: Enter the client name: x" onmouseover="alert(document.cookie)" y=" then press Add line. The rendered anchor becomes <a href="#" title="x" onmouseover="alert(document.cookie)" y="">, and hovering it runs the script. Today only the user typing the value is exposed. It becomes stored XSS the moment client names come from an API, an import or a paste.
remediation: Escape " and ' as " and ' in escapeHtml, or build the nodes with createElement, textContent and setAttribute so no string reaches innerHTML.
fix: not offerable: unbalanced brackets or quotes

title: Each client name is a link to # that goes nowhere
evidence: The anchor has href="#" and no handler. It is a tab stop and is announced as a link. Clicking it jumps to the page top and changes the URL hash. Its title repeats the visible text. Traced.
failing_case: Tab through the list: every line stops on a link that does nothing; clicking one scrolls to the top.
remediation: Render the name as plain text, or give the link a real target.

title: A whitespace-only client passes the required attribute and is stored as an empty name
evidence: The browser's required check accepts " ". The code trims afterwards and does not re-check, so client is "". The line then renders as an empty link (app.js:8). Traced.
failing_case: Type three spaces in Client, quantity 1, price 5, press Add line: a line with an empty client is added and posted.
remediation: After the trim, return with an error message if client is empty.

title: The live region is rebuilt wholesale with innerHTML on every add
evidence: render() replaces all children of #lines each time (app.js:7). Screen readers may re-announce the whole list on each add instead of only the new line. Traced, not tested with a screen reader.
failing_case: With 10 lines present, add an 11th: some screen readers read all 11 again.
remediation: Append only the new li, or announce a short message such as "Line added: Acme, 2 x 5.00" in a separate role=status element.
